questions.q: What is Oracle Net, per this lesson?
options: A backup and recovery utility
A background process that writes redo log entries to disk
Oracle's networking layer that carries client connection requests to a database server and results back (formerly called SQL*Net)
The tool used to create a new database
questions.explain: Oracle Net is the network layer underneath every client tool — SQL*Plus, SQL Developer, application drivers — used to reach a database.

questions.q: What is the purpose of tnsnames.ora, per this lesson?
options: A server-side file listing all database users and their passwords
The file that defines an Oracle instance's SGA size
A backup catalog listing RMAN backup pieces
A client-side file mapping a short net service name to a full connect descriptor (host, port, service name)
questions.explain: tnsnames.ora lets a client use a short alias like orclpdb instead of typing out a full host/port/service connection string.

questions.q: What does the Oracle Net Listener (tnslsnr) do, and what port does it listen on by default?
options: It listens exclusively on port 1433, the same as SQL Server
It runs only during database creation and then shuts down permanently
It's a client-side utility for browsing schema objects, with no fixed port
It's a server-side process that listens for incoming connection requests, on port 1521 by default
questions.explain: The listener process runs on the database server and listens on port 1521 by default, handing off incoming requests to the target instance.

questions.q: How does a running instance typically make the listener aware of its services, per this lesson?
options: The listener has no way of knowing which services exist
Dynamically — the instance's PMON process registers its services with the listener automatically
Through tnsnames.ora, the same file the client uses
Manually — a DBA must always add a static entry to listener.ora for every database
questions.explain: PMON dynamically registers a running instance's services with the listener, so a static listener.ora entry often isn't even required.

questions.q: In the connection flow described in this lesson, what happens immediately after the client resolves a net service name via tnsnames.ora?
options: The client bypasses the listener and connects directly to the SGA
The client connects to the listener on the resolved host and port
The instance immediately creates a new pluggable database
DBCA runs to create a new service
questions.explain: After resolving the connect descriptor, the client reaches the listener on that host/port, which then hands the connection off to the instance.
